summary: Phase 2 (Multi-Vendor + Plan Gating) backend testing complete. Created /app/backend/tests/test_vendor_phase2.py with 32 tests covering the full vendor lifecycle (onboarding validation, role sync, moderation, self-patch, document upload, plan info) plus plan gating (vendor quota, domain quota) and Phase 1 regression checks. All 32 Phase 2 tests pass. Also fixed a legitimate Phase 1 regression: TestCustomDomain in test_super_admin_tenants.py created its tenant with plan=free, which now correctly blocks domain adds under Phase 2 gating — updated the fixture to plan=enterprise so Phase 1 remains valid. Combined suite: 64/64 tests pass on 3 consecutive runs.

minor.issue: Empty types (payload {types: []}) returns 400 correctly, but the message is 'Pilih minimal 1 tipe vendor'. Ordering of type validation vs empty check works as intended.

Domain quota check runs BEFORE domain-format validation. When plan quota is exhausted, submitting an invalid or duplicate domain returns 403 (quota) instead of 400 (format). Not a bug, but worth noting for API consumers.

action_items: No blocking action items — Phase 2 backend is production-ready per specified requirements.
Optional: consider validating domain format BEFORE plan quota check so invalid inputs return 400 even when quota exhausted.
Optional: consider raising a clear 400 (not 422) for empty 'types' list to make client parsing easier — currently returns 400 correctly, so this is already fine.
critical_code_review_comments: routers/vendors.py:82 _sync_user_roles — silently no-ops when user record missing; consider logging so onboarding-role-drift is detectable.
routers/vendors.py:253 — document oversize check reads full body into memory before size check; for 5MB cap this is acceptable, but consider streaming for future limits >20MB.
core/plans.py:check_domain_quota — invoked BEFORE format validation in tenants.py:add_domain (line 248 vs 250). If plan quota exceeded, format errors are masked. Low risk.
server.py:ensure_official_vendor — idempotent create is correct; the trip back-fill uses updateMany with {'vendor_id': {'$exists': false}} so is safe on re-runs.
routers/tenants.py:377 super_list_vendors — enriches each vendor with user_email via N+1 queries. For >100 vendors this becomes slow; consider a $lookup aggregation.
routers/vendors.py:189 my_vendor — computes stats via N+1 (find all trip ids then two aggregate/count queries). Acceptable for small vendors, slow for large ones.
